kurz: Fish flesh is more delicate than the meat of land animals: short muscle fibres, little connective tissue, and protein that cooks at low temperatures.
bild_im_kopf: Like a book of thin pages only loosely stuck together: with too much heat it falls apart.
was_passiert: Fish does not have to work against gravity, so it has little connective tissue. The protein cooks from about 50 °C and quickly turns dry and crumbly with too much heat.
warum_wichtig: Fish forgives little overcooking. Gentle heat and a hot, dry pan for the skin are the two tools.
faustregeln: Better off the heat too early than too late.
Pat the skin dry and fry skin side down.
